concept: An intimate close-up of a composed face. The camera arcs and reveals the face is a thin surface with no head behind it, only depth: a vast black-stone hall where the person walks away. The camera pulls back until the gap is enormous, then follows the person into a warm, complex interior the surface never showed. The surface stays exactly where it was. The film returns to the face.
core_metaphor: The face you see every day is a surface. Behind it is a whole world you have never been inside.
character: The same person in every cast shot: an adult woman in her late thirties with deep brown skin, short natural hair and a composed, neutral expression, wearing a charcoal crew-neck sweater
recurring_element: one thin, slightly translucent face-surface holding a composed expression, and the vast black-stone hall with hairline gold veins that opens behind it
material: Black stone with hairline antique-gold (#C6A94F) veining; the face-surface like fine porcelain, slightly translucent at its edges; warm gold interior light against cool dusk light in the hall
primary_prompt: Restrained photorealistic 9:16 film about one face that turns out to be a thin surface with a vast world behind it. Close-ups of a calm adult face, a black-stone hall with hairline antique-gold (#C6A94F) veins, and a warm, lived-in interior at its end. Slow, physically credible camera, real light. No lettering, no horror, no cracks, no lens flares, no floating objects.

hook.text: You can see someone every day... and mistake it for knowing them.
hook.visual: Intimate close-up at eye level of an adult woman in her late thirties with deep brown skin, short natural hair and a composed, neutral expression, wearing a charcoal crew-neck sweater. Soft warm key light from the left, deep near-black background (#1A1A1A). Real skin texture, a natural catchlight, calm eyes looking just past the lens. The face fills most of the frame and reads at phone size. Nothing unusual is visible yet. No lettering, no glow, no masks, no makeup effects. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain. Motion: Very slow camera move to the right, already moving on the first frame. She blinks once and breathes; her expression stays composed and does not change. The background stays dark. Her face does not change shape. No new people.

build.text: You know their voice, their laugh, the way they cross a room. Familiarity hides distance well.
build.visual: The same woman's face seen from a three-quarter angle behind and to the side: the face is an extraordinarily thin, slightly translucent surface, like fine porcelain, holding the same composed expression. There is no head behind it. Past its edge opens a vast dark hall of black stone (#1A1A1A) with hairline antique-gold (#C6A94F) veins, and far down the hall a small figure in a charcoal sweater walks away from the surface. Strong depth. The surface is calm and beautiful, not eerie. No cracks, no horror, no lettering. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain. Motion: Slow camera arc to the left around the surface. The face-surface holds completely still with the same expression. Far down the hall the small figure keeps walking away at an even pace. The architecture does not change shape. No new people.

pivot.text: What someone lets you see, and who they are when no one is watching, are not always the same.
pivot.visual: Wide view down an immense black-stone hall (#1A1A1A) with hairline antique-gold (#C6A94F) veins. In the near foreground, small at the lower left, the thin translucent face-surface stands upright on its own, facing away from the hall. Far in the distance, a small figure in a charcoal sweater walks toward a faint warm light. The gap between the surface and the figure is enormous. Cool dusk light, fine dust in the air. No lettering, no portals, no glow halos. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain. Motion: Slow, steady pull-back down the hall. The surface in the foreground stays still and grows smaller. The distant figure keeps walking toward the warm light. Dust drifts. The architecture does not change shape. No new people.

resolution.text: You can know every expression on a face and still never see what lives behind it.
resolution.visual: A vast warm interior at the end of a black-stone hall: tiers of rooms, a wall of books, a long wooden table with a coat, plants and open notebooks, a tall window with green garden light, a staircase rising into gold (#C6A94F) light, bone-white (#F5F2EB) highlights. Small in the middle ground, a woman in a charcoal sweater stands in the light, seen from behind, at ease. Beautiful, lived-in, warm and complex. No lettering, no faces, no lens flares. Restrained, photorealistic, natural film grain. Motion: Slow push-in toward the warm interior. The woman turns her head slightly toward the window light. Soft light shifts across the shelves. The architecture does not change shape. No new people.

mobius_close.visual: The same intimate close-up as the opening: an adult woman in her late thirties with deep brown skin, short natural hair and a composed, neutral expression, wearing a charcoal crew-neck sweater, composed, against near-black (#1A1A1A), warm key light from the left. Motion: From the approved clip 1 still: very slow camera move to the left that eases to a stop on the opening framing. She blinks once; her expression stays composed. The background stays dark. No new people.

transitions.how: Hold the outline of the face in the same place across the cut; the incoming arc is already moving, so the face becomes a surface without a visible edit.
Align the faint warm light at the far end of the hall across the cut as the camera starts pulling back.
The warm light at the end of the hall blooms to fill the frame and settles into the interior.
0.4 s down to near-black and back up on the face. Change of place, not of mood; never pure black.
Clip 5 ends on clip 1's opening framing, so the loop has no fade.

universal_viewer_check.test: Could someone who knows nothing about the creator say every line about their own life?
entry_points: The person who realizes they never really knew someone they see every day.
The person who keeps a whole life behind a familiar face.
Partners, parents of adult children, old friends, colleagues: anyone who has confused familiarity with understanding.
universal_viewer_check.changes_for_this_law: No I, me, my or your in the narration. The closing line is a principle ('Presence is not access') rather than a declaration aimed at someone ('My presence is not your access'). The cast is a woman, distinct from the creator, so viewers don't read it as autobiography.

caption:
You can see someone every day and mistake it for knowing them.

How much do you know about the people you see every day?

Presence is not access.
